title: Nevanlinna theory of the Hahn difference operators and its applications: the second main theorem for Hahn difference operators
author: Ling Wang, Jianren Long, Xuxu Xiang
work: Nevanlinna theory of the Hahn difference operators and its applications
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem (source0.tex lines 268--278, source label thm2.5), the second main theorem for the Hahn difference operator: for a non-constant meromorphic function of zero order and distinct points of the complex plane, the defect inequality relating the Nevanlinna characteristic to the counting functions of the Hahn difference operator holds outside a set of logarithmic density zero; delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 279--318 (one adjacent proof environment of 40 lines that opens and closes inside the retained span). The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span together with its retained context: it applies the article's earlier theorem for the Hahn difference operator to obtain the intermediate defect estimate, estimates the counting functions of the shifted values through the logarithmic derivative lemma for the Hahn operator, controls the exceptional set by the logarithmic density argument, and combines the estimates into the stated second main theorem. This theorem is the main result of the article's second section and the tool through which its applications to value distribution are derived. H2: a research-level complex-analysis theorem in Nevanlinna theory whose proof combines the Hahn difference operator calculus, the logarithmic derivative lemma in the Hahn setting, counting-function estimates and an exceptional-set argument; it is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
